REAL OR FAKE?the toolkitOverview
The answer

Scammers don't build tricks.
They build trust.

Scams succeed because they look and sound like the real thing. AI makes the real thing cheap to copy. Tonight, four fakes:

1A voice you know, on the phone, saying words it never said
2A face you trust, on video, endorsing something fake
3A website that looks real, showing you numbers that are drawn on the screen
4A game that looks like fun; the fake casino scam moving through NT communities right now
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety03 / 19
FAKE 1voicesVoice cloning
Fake 1 · A voice you know

A few seconds of audio is enough to clone a voice

Where they get the voice

You already published it

A birthday video on Facebook. A voicemail greeting. A TikTok. A few seconds of clear speech is all the software needs, and most of us have posted years of it.

What they do with it

It says anything, live

The cloned voice can speak any words the scammer types, in real time, on a phone call. It laughs, hesitates and sounds stressed on demand.

The voice is no longer proof of who is talking. That is a hard sentence to accept about someone you love, and it is now simply true.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety04 / 19
A YARNbased on real Australian casesVoice cloning
Based on real cases; names and places changed

Nan's phone rings after tea. It's her grandson's voice; she'd know it anywhere. "Nan, I'm in trouble in Darwin. I need $800 for bail money tonight. Please don't tell Mum." He sounds frightened. He tells her exactly which store to go to and how to send it.

The grandson was home in Mparntwe the whole time, asleep. His voice came from a football video posted online. The fear in her chest was real; the voice was not.

ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety05 / 19
FAKE 1what beats itVoice cloning
What beats it

Hang up. Ring them back on the number you already have.

1Hang up and call back on the number saved in your phone; the clone cannot answer the real person's phone
2Set a family safe word; a word only your mob knows, that any caller asking for money must say
3Being rushed is the tell. "Tonight", "right now", "don't tell anyone" is pressure, and pressure is the scam
4Ask something only the real person would know that has never been posted online
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety06 / 19
FAKE 2faces and videoDeepfakes
Fake 2 · A face you trust

AI can put any words in any mouth

The classic

The famous face ad

A video of a well-known presenter, politician or finance expert warmly endorsing an investment platform. The face is real, the footage is real; the words were never said.

Why it works

Borrowed authority

We trust the endorsement because we trust the person. Scammers rent that trust for the cost of a video clip, and place the ad on the same social feeds as real news.

Rule of thumb: a celebrity who genuinely endorses an investment will be on the company's official website and in mainstream news, not only in a social media ad.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety07 / 19
A YARNbased on real Australian casesDeepfakes
Based on real cases; names and places changed

A pensioner sees a video of a famous economist recommending an investment platform. She does the right things: she watches it twice, she visits the website, it looks professional. She starts small. A friendly "account manager" moves the chat to WhatsApp. Her dashboard shows her money growing week after week.

The video was a deepfake. The dashboard was a picture of profits, drawn on the screen by the scammers. When she tried to withdraw, there was suddenly a "tax" to pay first, then a "release fee", then silence. $76,000; her savings.

ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety08 / 19
RED FLAGthe platform switchDeepfakes
The red flag hiding in that story

If the chat wants to move,
that's the scam moving

"Let's continue on WhatsApp" sounds friendly. What it actually does:

1Moves you away from the platform's scam detection and report buttons
2Moves you into an encrypted, private channel where nobody else can see the grooming
3Makes the relationship feel personal and special; that feeling is the product
A business you have never met that wants to leave the app you met on is a scam until proven otherwise. Banks, brokers and government agencies do not run your account through WhatsApp.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety09 / 19
FAKE 3websitesSpoofed sites
Fake 3 · A website that looks real

Copying a real website takes minutes, not months

The clone

Same look, wrong address

Scammers copy a bank or shop site pixel for pixel. The only honest thing left on the page is the address bar; read it slowly.

The padlock myth

The padlock is not approval

The browser padlock means the connection is private. It says nothing about who is on the other end; scam sites have padlocks too.

The drawn-on screen

Screens can lie

Balances, profits, "reviews", even urgent virus warnings can simply be drawn on the page. A number on a screen is not money.

Habit that beats all three: never follow the link you were sent. Type the address yourself, or search the organisation's name together with the word "scam" first.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety10 / 19
HERE, NOWfake online casinosScambling
Fake 4 · The one aimed at NT communities right now

"Scambling": the casino game
that is not a casino

What it looks like

Bright, friendly, familiar

A colourful pokies-style game, shared on Facebook or WhatsApp; often the link comes from someone you know who is playing it too. That is the trap: it arrives through trust, not from a stranger.

Facebook message · from a cousin
Sis try this one, I won $250 last night!! Free credits when u sign up, this one actually pays. [link]
The site is not a licensed casino. It is a scam operation, often overseas, using geo-targeting to reach remote communities; and it never intends to pay out.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety11 / 19
HERE, NOWhow the hook worksScambling
How the hook works

Free credits, small wins,
then the door closes

1Free credits to start; the game is genuinely fun, and the first small "wins" come easily
2Your "balance" grows; but when you try to withdraw, you must deposit real money first to "unlock" it
3The winnings never arrive. Instead: more deposits, more conditions, or "recruit your friends and family" to unlock
4That recruiting step is why it moves through families and communities; every player is pushed to become the next messenger

People are losing money for food and power, and going into debt; and feeling ashamed to tell anyone. Shame is part of the scam's design.

ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety13 / 19
HERE, NOWthe rule, and the yarn to haveScambling
One rule, one yarn

A casino that won't pay out is not a casino

The rule

Withdrawal is the test

Real licensed gambling pays out winnings; that is the whole deal. A site that keeps inventing reasons you can't withdraw is not a casino, it's a scam; stop putting money in.

The yarn to have

No shame, just stop the money

"You haven't done anything wrong; that game was built to do this to people. Let's stop the deposits, screenshot everything, and report it together. Plenty of mob got caught by this one."

If money is owed or bills are behind because of it: Mob Strong Debt Help, 1800 808 488; free legal advice and financial counselling for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, anywhere in Australia.
ntworld.inkAI & Cyber Safety14 / 19
FAKE + PATIENCEthe long gameRomance baiting
The long game · "romance baiting"

The cruellest scams are slow

Weeks or months of friendship or romance first; the money talk comes late, and by then it doesn't feel like a stranger asking.

1A friendly message out of nowhere; often a "wrong number" or a new online friend, then the chat moves to WhatsApp
2Daily attention, real warmth, no requests at all; this stage is the investment
3Then a casual mention of crypto "investing", small amounts first, a dashboard showing profits; the same drawn-on screen as before

First Nations investment scam losses reached $4.1 million in 2025, up 162.7% in a year. (NASC Targeting Scams 2025, March 2026)

DEFENCEthree words to rememberStop · Check · Protect
The national advice, three words

Stop. Check. Protect.

Stop

Pressure is the tell

Scammers rush you so you can't think. Real organisations can wait while you take your time; anyone who can't wait is the scam.

Check

Could this be fake?

Never click the link you were sent. Find the organisation yourself, from its official website or app, and ring back on the number you already have.

Protect

Act fast if it feels wrong

Contact your bank first if money or details have gone, then report it. Acting quickly is what recovers money; embarrassment can wait.

Same three words as the Little Book of Scams; everything in that book is still true. Tonight was what's happened since it was printed.

Report it, and get real help

Bank first. Then report and recover.

1Your bank, immediately, if money has moved or card details are out; ring the number on the back of your cardFIRST
2Scamwatch, scamwatch.gov.au; reports can be made anonymously, or on behalf of someone elseREPORT
3IDCARE, 1800 595 160; free help when identity details have been stolenIDENTITY
4Mob Strong Debt Help, 1800 808 488; free legal and financial counselling for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peopleMONEY
5National Debt Helpline, 1800 007 007; free financial counselling for anyoneMONEY
"On behalf of someone else" matters here. If an Elder or family member won't ring anyone, you can report for them.

The real close

The warnings don't reach your communities.
You do.

Official reporting from remote communities is low; the algorithms don't carry these warnings to the people who need them. A yarn from someone trusted does what no government campaign can. Take the handouts; give them away.
